utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. Accused Colonel Beara is not present today. The Trial Chamber has been informed that he is indisposed. I take it that there is a waiver, Mr. Ostojic, if you could kindly confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There is, Your Honour. We met with him this morning, and he wasn't feeling well but he was going to the nurses and the UND said that they were going to provide all the necessary forms to you, and he has orally given me the authorisation to proceed in his absence with this witness and perhaps the next one tomorrow, because it's in the morning session, he may not recover that quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ostojic. And from the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon, and Mr. Haynes. All right. From Prosecution I notice the presence of Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Nicholls, Mr. Elderkin, and no one else behind the column. The witness is present. Witness, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. You don't need to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to repeat the solemn declaration that you made yesterday to testify the truth. It's still valid and will continue to be valid throughout your entire testimony. All right. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should tell the Chamber and the witness the matter that caused that rather unseemly scene in court yesterday has been resolved, and I'm grateful to my learned friends who have been very cooperative and I will deal with this in due course, not with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is about the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. A great deal of time is going to be saved as a result of my learned friend's cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Mr. McCloskey or Mr. Elderkin, I don't know who you negotiated with, and yourself, Mr. Josse. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Witness, before we return to the document that I was in the middle of cross-examining you about yesterday, I would like to go back slightly in time and look at one other document that I should have perhaps asked about yesterday and it's 6D69, please. This is a report, in effect, from Mr. Sahic to the Sarajevo services centre dated we can see the 16th of February, 1994, and it's the very last page, please, that I'd like to look at, page 2 in the B/C/S, page 3 in the English. Towards the bottom of the page, please, that's fine, thank you. After the numerated items we see, and I'm reading from the middle of that next paragraph, "All members of the Zepa SJB are organised into a police war manoeuvre unit which, within the Zepa demilitarised zone, carries out tasks envisaged by the binding instructions of the MUP of the republic on the organisation and tasks of the police during war and other extraordinary circumstances, as well as combat tasks in the defence of the free territory of Zepa municipality envisaged by the plan on the organisation tasks, engagement and works of units and the order of the commander of the Zepa municipality armed forces in the zone of responsibility assigned to the unit." What do you understand that to mean, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is just an information note. There were no activities and no tasks, apart from at the time of defence, since the police did have its zone of responsibility at that time. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Why do you think Mr. Sahic used the word "combat tasks in the defence of the free territory of Zepa municipality"? What did he mean by the words "combat tasks"?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I can't answer that question, it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Isn't this evidence that at the very least in early 1994 the SJB worked in conjunction with the Zepa Brigade on offensive manoeuvres against Serb targets outside of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during that period of time, because there were no offensive manoeuvres at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: In case I have misunderstood you, is there any period of time that you say the Zepa SJB worked in conjunction with the brigade in offensive manoeuvres?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So I don't want to labour the point, but is it wrong to read this document so as to suggest that the SJB were, in early 1994, involved in combat tasks?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you that there were no combat tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: One other part of the document I would like to direct your attention to, please, and it's the second paragraph on the first page. Mr. Sahic says, "Depending on war activities between 13 July 1992, when it was set up, and 24 November 1993, the Zepa SJB carried out tasks falling within its competence in the Zepa region participating in the defence of the free territory on a daily basis and performing the most difficult and complex combat tasks in the region and also elsewhere." What's Mr. Sahic talking about there, please, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with that. Since there was no action during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Of course the 24th of November of 1993 was after the demilitarisation of the zone, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Right. We'll move on and, if we may, move back to the document that I was asking you about yesterday, which is 6D82. And whilst it's being got up on the screen, you will remember that you were disputing my proposition that the Muslim defenders of the Zepa enclave had some -- had a greater degree of artillery weapons at their disposal than you were asserting. You remember you and I disagreeing about that yesterday, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And so far as the document is concerned, we had dealt with the barriers that you accept had been placed in Zepa for defensive purposes, and I had got to a point in the document which dealt with barriers using logs and stones. The next sentence, I'm going to summarise, basically the author of the report says there is a possibility that there may be some improvised MES, which apparently is mines and explosives and then I'll read on. "The Muslim forces have also incorporated UNPROFOR combat hardware and weapons which they obtained following the recent blockade and capture of the Ukrainian check-points into their defensive arsenal." Now, to be fair to you, I think you said early on in my cross-examination that you accept that weapons were seized by the defenders from UNPROFOR. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: All right. Deal with it a different way, because I am not in a position to check at the moment. The sentence I have just read to you from this report; do you agree with it?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I heard nothing about their weapons being used and whether they took them to the base, I don't know. I don't know what they did with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The report continues: "We believe that at least nine OT," which are the armoured personnel carriers, "with the accompanying weapons and ammunition are in the hands of Muslim soldiers." Did you see any armoured personnel carriers being used by the defenders?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Did you learn through any source as to whether armoured personnel carriers were being used by the defenders, as opposed to seeing it with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The next part of this report, if we could scroll down slightly, please, deals with firing positions which even the report says are only "conditionally accurate." And I am not going to go through those. Immediately beneath that it says, "In any case, for four days now the Muslims have been making their presence known with heavy 14.5 millimetre PAM." Do you know what a PAM is?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an anti-aircraft machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: They were being used by the defenders, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't, because they didn't have such weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You can categorically say, can you, that the information contained within this Drina Corps report is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct. At least not as far as this part that concerns the PAMs is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Let's go on. Deals with the reserve ammunition, I won't ask you about that. Then it says, "Likewise, coaxial 7.62-millimetre PM of the PKT type with around 40.000 rounds were probably also dismounted from the OT." Does that term, 7.62-millimetre PM, mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I'm familiar with that calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Were they being used by the defenders?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, perhaps one was captured at the beginning of the war. As far as the quantity of ammunition is concerned, there's nothing I can say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Let's go on. "The Ukrainian check-points also had 40-millimetre RBR of the RGP type" what are RBRs of the RGP type, please?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I really don't know what these abbreviations mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that they're hand-held rocket launchers? Did you see any of those being used?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The Drina Corps suggests that at least 120 of the rockets that go into such rocket launchers were in the enclave, left by UNPROFOR. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: What happened to the UNPROFOR hardware?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that their members stayed on after we had been evacuated. What subsequently happened to those things, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Are you aware of UNPROFOR being relieved of their weapons by the Muslims at all?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of anything being seized. All I know is that they had withdrawn from their check-points and gone to their base. Whether that was with their equipment and weapons or without those items, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Witness, if you say that the defenders didn't have the sort of weaponry described in this report, I repeat, in a different context, question I asked you yesterday: Why were the defenders able to repel the Serb attack for so long?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday, it was a matter of a fight for survival, the survival of the individuals concerned and of their families. They had to do their utmost to defend themselves and in the end they didn't succeed. What happened, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You have told us that because you were incapacitated you were not involved in police activity at all in July of 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether any of your police colleagues participated in the defence of the enclave in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that the police had its own zone of responsibility in the event of an attack and that was at Brezova Ravan.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, do you know offhand at what point Brezova Ravan fell into the hands of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a hundred per cent sure, but I think it was a day or two before the civilian population and the wounded were evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And was it at that point that the police were engaged with Serbian forces in trying to stop that post from falling?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And how do you know that, bearing in mind you were incapacitated and at your parents' home?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleagues who survived told me about this. That's how I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And what weapons did your colleagues use in trying to defend the post?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Which they had got from where?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From UNPROFOR, when they returned the weapons that had been taken at the beginning of the war, or rather in May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And have you any idea how your police colleagues defended that post, for several days at the very least, using automatic rifles against the light and heavy artillery at the disposal of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had dug in, the defence line had been established. They managed to hold the line right up until infantry attacks were launched. Once the infantry attacks were launched, the line gave way and Brezova Ravan fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Nearing the end, Witness. You, I take it, know nothing about the negotiations to evacuate the civilian population of the enclave. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: What do you know?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is what I heard about the result of the negotiations and about how the civilian population and the wounded were to be evacuated. As for the course of the negotiations, as to what happened up there, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And at the point that you left, what did you understand was going to happen to the armed Muslim men of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I didn't give that much thought at the time. I thought about myself, about how I would get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I just want to go back and ask you one thing I had been questioning you about a moment ago. And that is the area where your police colleagues were defending. How large was that area; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps between 100 and 150 metres long, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do you know where the nearest army unit was? Well, brigade unit was. I'm talking about defence brigade, in relation to where the policemen were?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were deployed on the left flank and on the right flank, but I don't know how close they were to each other, how close they were linked up, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do you know where the Luka unit, police unit, this is, were engaged, if at all?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that they were engaged. If they had been, they were on the terrain that they covered in practical terms, which was in the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: At the point that you left the enclave you had no idea, did you, what was going to happen to the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could only assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Who's next? Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness, how are you?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm well. And you yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Fine, thank you very much. Witness, do you know an individual by the name of Muhamed [sic] Hajric from Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mehmed Hajric, yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And could you tell me briefly what was his position at the time, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, Mr. Hajric was the president of the Presidency of Zepa municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in that position can you describe what his duties were?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't tell you, because I don't know. I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in the time-frame leading up to the evacuation in Zepa, did you -- do you recall personally speaking with him?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not speak with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Meek. Mr. Elderkin, before we run out of time, the -- let's go into private session. You may sit down, Mr. Meek, and follow what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Zivanovic, I understand you don't have any cross-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I won't have any cross-examination for this witness either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, madam. Mr. Lazarevic or Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have no cross-examination for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Madam Fauveau. Or sorry. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could you just bear with me for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I hope that we will agree that combat activities around Srebrenica or attacks, depending on the angle, started on the 14th of July, 1995. Do we agree? I apologise, I'm talking about Zepa, actually.

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In your statement you stated that the convoys stopped arriving some month or month and a half before the attacks. Did I understand your statement well?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did. But I'm not a hundred per cent sure about that either. When I provided my statement I said that as far as I can remember, this was in late May or early June, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at document 5D229. Mr. President, the document that the Defence is going to show to the witness are in Serbian only, and it is -- it -- they are all being translated at the moment, and I apologise for this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the document which was issued on the 17th of June, 1995? Yesterday you saw a similar document, but not the same one. This was issued by the brigadier of the 2nd Corps of the BiH army. His name is Sulejman Budakovic. It was sent to the command of the 285th Light Brigade Zepa, RLBR Zepa. In the introduction of this document it says that, "Pursuant to an oral order by the commander of the general staff of the BiH army, on the occasion of great successes that the units of the ABiH army have achieved in the general sector of Sarajevo and Gorazde, and pursuant to the intelligence according to which the command of the AS protection regiment in Han Pijesak keep in reserve some of the troops in order to intervene in case of an attack by our forces from Zepa." Do you know, did you hear of this protection regiment unit in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never heard this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And do you know that in Han Pijesak there was the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Further on in this order do you see under item 1 that this order was issued in order to inflict losses upon the aggressor forces and that there should be cooperation with the AR BiH, which are carrying out operations in the Sarajevo sector. Did you know that there was combat around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard it on the radio and this is all I knew, I heard it on the news.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Further on, under item 2 of this order, can you see that the order is issued in order to plan realistic tasks by which success will be achieved based on the true assessment and the true capabilities of our forces in Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please call document 227. I apologise, this is 5D227. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document was issued on the 28th of June, 1995. Can you see that? And on page 2 of this document, could we please go to page 2? Thank you. You can see that the document was signed by Colonel Avdo Palic. Can we go back to the front page of the document, please? Under item 1 of this document it -- could you please scroll up? We are actually talking about the first paragraph of the document. It's okay now. It says, "Pursuant to the order by the acting commander of the 28th Division of Srebrenica, Major Ramiz Becirevic, in connection with the order issued on the 20th of June, 1995, I am taking measures in order to carry out sabotage operations with a view to inflicting losses on the aggressor, on the aggressor's troops and equipment, and the overall prevention from Chetniks accessing Sarajevo." Pursuant to this order, the goal is to deter the enemy forces from approaching Srebrenica, Zepa and ultimately Sarajevo. Is that the case or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says on the paper. But what the factual situation was, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness, if we briefly go back to the previous document issued the 17th of June, do you remember what it contained?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In that document the attacks are also mentioned, and also combat activities around Sarajevo. Can we then conclude that these documents, actually the latter document, the second document, is consistent with the previous one, or rather that the second document is just to implement the order of a higher command?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we now scroll up the document in order to show the numbers from 1 to 9, so can you scroll down? Excellent. Thank you. Sir, in the middle of this document you can see numbers from 1 to 9. Can you see them?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sabotage groups are mentioned here. That from the sectors of Zepa and Srebrenica attack roads and facilities in the area of Zlebovi [phoen] Pecnik near Han-Kram, will we agree that this is the main road or the regional road connecting Vlasenica with Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's rather Sokolac Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Okay. So Sokolac Han Pijesak. You have anticipated my next question. Under number 2, Romanija Sokolac, the same road is mentioned. And the administrative building on the road to Sokolac, and also Zlebovi Pecnik is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't know where that building is, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Under 8 you can see that a reference is made to a place called Karaule [phoen], which is on that same road, the road from Vlasenica to Sokolac?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that sector at all. I don't know where that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In any case, we have agreed that these operations were taking place on that road between Vlasenica and Sokolac?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Based on this report, therefore, and could we know scroll down the document just a little? Yes. You can see that in the last paragraph a reference is made to the fact that about 40 Chetniks were killed, dozens of them were wounded, a significant amount of equipment was captured, and so on and so forth. Can you see that as part of this combat report?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: One can then conclude, based on this report, that on this road combat operations were going on? Sir, did you hear my question? Or do I have to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I am not -- I'm not clear on what you were asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this: Will you agree with me that the Vlasenica-Sokolac road was the place of certain combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says on this paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that in the area of combat operations usually the movement of vehicles is somewhat restricted?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What zone are you referring to, the same zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The same zone, from Vlasenica to Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, it must have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would you then agree with me -- I apologise. Would you agree with me that if a convoy which leaves Zvornik to arrive in Rogatica and Zepa, it has to go through Vlasenica, Han Pijesak and Sokolac?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the road that such a convoy would use.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, you have told us that some of the humanitarian aid, and you correct me if I'm wrong, please, some 12 per cent was allocated for the army. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: As you were doing your job, when it comes to the goods from the humanitarian aid, could you find those on the black market which existed in all of the enclaves, primarily in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some little quantities of salt and some flour could be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I assume that you know who defined that percentage of 12 per cent that had to be allocated for the army?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was the Executive Board or the municipal assembly, but in any case, it was one or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the person called Enver Stitkovac whose nickname was Zuco?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that he was maybe the main wheeler and dealer on the black market?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree on that but he did not deal in the goods from the humanitarian aid. He sold other types of goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What did he trade in?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cigarettes, fuel, salt, those were his staple goods. Some chocolate for the children maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please call up document number 5D223.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness, this document was issued by the chief of the public security station, Hurim Sahic. In the letterhead of that document it says public security station, Zepa, the date is 4th of April, 1995. In the first paragraph of this document it says as follows: "The check-point of the public security station of Zepa was put up on the Zepa-Rogatica road in a place called Brezova Ravan at the entrance to the demilitarised zone of Zepa. In the vicinity of that check-point is the check-point manned by UNPROFOR." Yesterday, in the course of your testimony you told us that the check-point had indeed been set up in order to check the goods and people entering Zepa. We can then agree that this is what you said?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, line 4, it says this: "However, the police manning the check-point have infantry and anti-armour weapons which are used for the implementation of the combat task that was given to the public security station of Zepa on the order of the commander to 85 IBLBR on the defence of the free territory of Zepa. The aforementioned weapons are kept away from the UNPROFOR and members of other UN organisations in order not to put the security of the zone at risk." Sir, were you ever at this check-point, as part of your duties?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You were aware of the existence of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In this document, further down under item 3 it says, "On the 30th of March, 1995, an UNPROFOR convoy was controlled at the Brezova Ravan check-point in the Kamaz vehicle, registration number" such-and-such, goods were found that weren't part of the convoy. Goods which were taken from the owner, Major Sergej, with a certificate, and he was informed that these goods would be returned to him when the convoy left the zone. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you also aware of the fact that on that occasion, on the 30th of March, the black market goods, these black market goods were kept, 100 kilograms of coffee, 364 pieces of chocolate, bars of chocolate, 75 lighters, 1.789 packets of rolling paper?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So we will agree that all of these goods were goods that were unavailable on the Zepa market, and later it was sold for far greater price than is usual on that market?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, at the time of this event, did Mr. Sahic, inform the MUP, the ministry of the interior in Sarajevo, on the very same date, about 8.00 p.m. at the Brezova Ravan check-point, a vehicle arrived and this UNPROFOR major called Sergej got out of the vehicle, as well as Enver Stitkovac, also known as Zuco, who permanently resided in Zepa. Are you aware of the fact that they arrived at that check-point?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Stitkovac used a weapon to threaten people and take those goods away to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You also do not dispute the fact that your colleagues did not intervene, they did not make use of the weapons that were concealed somewhere at the check-point?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And you also don't dispute the fact that Stitkovac enjoyed the protection of the civilian and military leadership, in addition -- and in spite of the fact that the police reported to the court, and the prosecutor's office, he was never prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. And in addition to that support, UNPROFOR also supported and protected him because he worked with them and for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Your superior, or I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I used the term "your superior" and I wasn't thinking about the fact that that might reveal the identity of -- very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me consult with the Prosecution. I personally don't have problems, none of the other judges. Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I don't think so, given what's come out already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Petrusic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljic then says that when assessing the phenomenon of illegal trading in Zepa, he claims that the best way to prevent such crime is to control individuals, vehicles and goods at the entrance into Zepa, with the objective of preventing them from bringing in goods for the black market. Are you aware of the fact that he informed his superiors about his way of controlling the situation?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But if he informed anyone, he informed people who were his superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the next page of this document, please. Let's have a look at item 4. You don't dispute the fact that this is what is stated in the document?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we please tender 5D5237.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Could we see it, please."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague has just told me that we have this document in English too. Could we have a look at the last two paragraphs. We can leave it like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, as you can see, this document has been forwarded by the SJB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it the number should read 237?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 237, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because in the transcript, in case you're not following Judge Kwon, in the transcript you have Exhibit 5D5237, and that is an unlikely number in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, as you can see, this document was forwarded by the Zepa public security station to the Security Services Centre in Sarajevo. To the chief of that service the assistant minister of the -- of -- of the interior, Momir Stanovic, issued the document. Please let's have a look at the last two paragraphs. The penultimate paragraph, Witness, reads as follows: "Authorised officials have the duty to take measures and organise activities in order to detect crimes that relate to bringing in 40 or rather goods that are not sufficiently supplied and that are intended for the black market. These measures shall not be taken at check-points but in areas where these elicit activities are, in fact, being carried out." Witness, would you agree with me that the assistant minister, Omer Stambolic is suggesting to the chief of the public security station in Zepa that he should not control anything at the check-point, the check-point which was established, but he should do so -- he should carry out checks, once these goods have been distributed, once they start distributing the goods on the market?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So that would be counter to any kind of logic, police logic or any other kind of logic, when it comes to crime prevention. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One correction. Perhaps my phrasing of the question was awkward, but the document we are referring to was sent to the deputy minister of the interior from Sarajevo to the chief of the SJB in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph in this document, Witness, is the following stated -- just a minute. Does it state that acting counter to the suggestion of the assistant minister, could result in the supply of humanitarian aid being interrupted? Sir, do you have an explanation as to why establishing a check-point and as to why controlling goods at the check-point could result in cutting off the supply of humanitarian aid? Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goods that were being controlled had nothing to do with the supply of humanitarian aid. There was no direct link between the two, so I find this illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 5D233, please. We'll just have a quick look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You can see that the heading of the document mentions the 285th IBLBR Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The signatory of this document is Zuco, and I believe we will agree that this is Enver Stitkovac?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: By this telegram he informs a certain Suljo in the command of the 28th division in Srebrenica that the price of oil was four German marks and petrol, five German marks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says, however this was much more expensive on the market itself, in realistic terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In other words, Stitkovac, Enver Stitkovac, Zuco, also supplied the army, the 28th Division, with different types of fuel? Is that correct? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says on this piece of paper, but I didn't know that. I was unaware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The last sentence in this telegram which says that the telegram was sent with the approval of the command of the 285th IBLBR. Does it corroborate the fact that he enjoyed the trust of many people, including the commander of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up document 5D241.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you look at the heading of this document, and if you see that this document was issued a day after the previous document that we saw, and that -- that it was sent to Zuco from Srebrenica, it is clear that this document is talking about the sale that was also mentioned in the previous document. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness, you performed the duties, correct me if I'm wrong, as of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the crime prevention department, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in that job?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the beginning of June or the end of May, until I was hospitalised in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about illegal trade before you became an operative in the police?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, just partly. Because all of these things were done with the mediation of UNPROFOR. All the goods were taken over from their check-points, or from their main base.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at 5D31. The ERN number is 5027. These are the last digits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher, I think it's two pages further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5027. Thank you. Excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English version is 5015.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please look at number 3, the person mentioned is Nedzad Bektic?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I assume that you know that he was the assistant commander for security in the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, but I heard of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In this report it says that in late 1992 and early 1993, Bektic sold wheat in Zepa that was war booty or people provided it for the army. At the time a hundred grams [as interpreted] of wheat was sold at 2.000 German marks. Do you know anything about illegal trade in cereals?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know something, but not in the way you interpret it. At that time people went to Srebrenica from Zepa to buy food, but not seeds for sowing, just foods, cereal for food.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to correct something. On page 27, 11 -- line 11, instead of gram, it should read kilogram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know whether the convoys of humanitarian aid, since we're talking about seeds, cereal seeds, also carried those cereal seeds?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as cereal seeds, but potato seeds and some vegetables like tomato and peppers and similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Zepa and its surroundings i.e. the protected area of Zepa was primarily rural area, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And people primarily engaged in farming before the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, farming and cattle-breeding were the main sources of income.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us yesterday that you were never awarded or decorated for your work. Are you familiar with an initiative on the part of the chief of security, Mr. Sahic, on the 6th of April, which was the official day of the Security Services, the collegium of the public security station in Zepa proposed to the MUP to decorate you for your achievements and your work?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just me, but some other people as well. My colleagues. But this all boiled down to that request, or sent to the ministry of interior in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you this request, or proposal. This is document 5D218. Can I call this document up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I don't think it's necessary to show it, because the document contains information that should not be made public.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is the suggestion for an award and you say that it never came to anything, it was just a suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Have a look after item 7. Please scroll down a bit. It says a particular award to be conferred on a policeman and then there is an illegible part and it says then, "And Sabriju Kulovac, the son of Galiba born on the 25th of January, 1957, for the successfully having detected perpetrator of a crime committed against an UNHCR convoy on the 24th of August, 1994." At the time you were in the police force?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us were this occurred?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Zepa area, and it related, the event or incident related to the misappropriation of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And the convoy transporting humanitarian aid was attacked?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't received interpretation, but if I understand you well, you wish to take the break now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Mr. President, I see we have another couple of minutes before the break, so I suggest we have the break now."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Meek has asked to be excused, and we have excused him. Give him permission to stay away. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness, we'll briefly deal with the relationship between your service and the army. In the course of your testimony yesterday -- well, could we see 6D49, page 5? My colleague Josse asked a question about this. Page 5, please. Yes. Could you scroll down a bit? I'd like to see the last paragraph. Witness, as you can see, the document was written on the 30th of April, 1994 by the SJB chief, Mr. Sahic. It was forwarded to the Supreme Command of the ABiH, to Rasim Delic, General Rasim Delic personally. In the last paragraph he says, "I am informing you that as soon as the war requires this, together with SJB members, I will take up the first combat positions and to date, this has practically been a daily activity for us." Do you have a comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no particular comment to make. But at the very beginning of the attack zone of responsibility was assigned to the members of the Zepa SJB, and the situation continued in that way until the very end?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: During this period of time, on the 30th of October --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: -- 1994, there was no combat activity on the part of the army of Republika Srpska, was there?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't, apart from sporadic fire, but this was quite rare.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we say that members of the Republika Srpska army respected the agreement on the safe haven?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the very same document, page 4. Yes, that's right. It's the second paragraph. Please return to the beginning of the document. The beginning of the page. Thank you. Have a look at paragraph 2 where Mr. Sahic says the following, and the document is addressed to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I quote: "It's my duty to inform you that the cause of such a situation is the objective and faulty information provided to the Presidency -- is the unobjective and the faulty information of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and its highest organs as well as the main committee of the SJN [as interpreted] in Sarajevo with regard to the situation in Zepa. And this was done by Avdo Palic, commander of the brigade that is present here, and Dr. Hajlic [phoen] Becir, president of the Repljak [phoen] Club in Sarajevo." Sir, could we agree that the conclusion that we could draw from this is that the commander of the Zepa Brigade, Avdo Palic, wasn't informing his superior command, the Main Staff of the ABiH, on the actual situation in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know what sort of reports it concerned. One should probably have to read through the entire document that given what is stated, well, it seems that that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The chief of the Security Service was being constantly obstructed, we will put it in this way, by the command and by the commander, Avdo Palic?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could one say that Mr. Palic was the be all and end all when it came to what happened in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a large extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we have a look at 5D225, 5D225. Sir, this document was issued by commander Sead Delic, a brigadier, and the heading says the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 2nd Corps command. So it was issued by its commander, in Tuzla on the 9th July 1995. It's addressed to the 28th Division and TO the command of the 285th East Bosnia Light Brigade in Zepa. The document states, "On the basis of your document highly confidential number 08-22-143/95 and with regard to taking weapons under UN control, I hereby order --" rather, I apologise. "By an order of the Main Staff of the ABiH highly confidential number 1/825-1010 dated the 9th of July, 1995 in item 3 it is explicitly ordered that weapons should be taken and the aggressor should be confronted by using all means at your disposal in order to protect the population." Do you know anything about this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's the first time I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that on the 9th of July no combat operations had commenced around Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 5D259.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the heading of the document. It says the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Zepa municipality, War Presidency, the date, 5th of May, 1995 addressed to the government of the Republic of the BiH federation in Sarajevo. It's for the attention of the minister, Dr. Hasan Muratovic. And it goes on to say that the subject of this document is social evacuation from Zepa. I'll quote part of document which states the following: "Out of the total number of inhabitants of Zepa, 65 per cent are refugees who, on the whole, came from the territory of the municipality of Han Pijesak, Rogatica, Visegrad and Vlasenica." Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would you also agree that -- or would you also agree with the fact mentioned that states the following: "Given the possibility for accommodation and the supply of food in Zepa, most of them live in very poor conditions. And it's necessary to emphasise the fact that some of the elderly and some women and children in other free areas of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, have sons, daughters and husbands who have appropriate accommodation, whose status has been regulated. That part of the population exerts pressure on the government in Zepa and they're asking for the possibility of being evacuated to other parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would you also agree that a request was made upon that population, or rather that that population requested that negotiations should be carried out at the local level with Serbian officer Milan Pacanac to discuss social evacuation from Zepa and that negotiations were scheduled for the 10th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that, this is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In any case you are not disputing the fact that there was a wish or rather an intention of the population that not hail from the territory of Zepa to be evacuated to other areas under the control of the BiH army where they had other members of their families residing?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see document 5D244.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the heading of the document you can see that the command of the 28th Division sent this document on the 27th of May, 1995, to the command of the 285th East Bosnian Light Infantry Brigade for the attention of the commander in Zepa. And this is an order. "The command of all units on the strength of the 28th Division of the army are duty-bound to take all the necessary measures in order to prevent members of the army and civilian persons in their intention to leave Srebrenica and Zepa." Do you know anything about this order?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday we touched upon this question. I don't know anything officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: It says further on in this order, "All necessary measures should be taken in order to prevent the departure of organised groups in the direction of Kladanj, Tuzla or Serbia. You are duty-bound to gather intelligence on individuals or groups which are getting ready to leave, and institute measures against such individuals, group in order to prevent their departure. You are also duty-bound to provide the command of the division and the Public Security Services about any such intelligence that you gather." Did your service ever receive this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it did. If it had, I'm sure that we would have been informed about this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the civilian population of Srebrenica and Zepa did go to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody from Zepa. And, as for Srebrenica, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 2nd of August, 1995, about 860 people left Zepa, they were all able-bodied men and they all went to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I apologise. Can you repeat the date once again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The 2nd August, and thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sir, as you are looking at this order, you can conclude that it is contrary to the wish expressed by the population of Zepa and Srebrenica who wanted to leave the area and join their families?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the departure for Serbia took place only after the fall of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The question was whether you knew that over 800 people left Zepa after the 2nd of August, and went to Serbia, and you said that you are aware of that. However, my next question was this: The order that we have just spoken about, dated 27 May, that you still have on the screen before you, was it contrary to the desire and wish expressed by the population of Zepa, in which 65 per cent were refugees, wanted to leave the area but were prevented from doing so? Actually, this order prevents people from leaving?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to a certain extent, in a certain way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at another document, please. 5D235.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the heading of this order dated 17 June, it says, "The command of the 28th Division," and this order was sent to the command of the 285th Zepa Brigade. In the first paragraph of this order it says as follows: "The command of the 285th IBLBR shall undertake all the necessary operative measures through the organs of military security of the brigade, and it will cooperate with the public security station of Zepa in order to prevent military persons and civilians from leaving the free territories of Srebrenica, Zepa, and from crossing over to the free territories of Kladanj and Tuzla. It will also prevent all attempts by these people to leave in the direction of Serbia." Did the command of the 285th Brigade ever deliver such an order to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Is this order also in contradiction with the wish expressed by the refugee population of Zepa to leave the area?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness, I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, this completes my cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Petrusic. That leaves us with the Pandurevic Defence teams. Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I have only a few questions. First of all, can you agree with me that Zepa fell on the 24th of July, and that is when the evacuation started?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was 12 years ago, you see, but I believe you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that the evacuation finished on the 27th of July of the same year?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you also agree -- could we please go into private session for my third question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Since you allow for the possibility that the evacuation started on the 24th of July, when Zepa fell, I would like to remind you that in your statement given to the OTP on the 23rd of March of this year, when you spoke about the fall of Zepa in item 6 you said this: "[In English] Zepa fell and the evacuations started." [Interpretation] Can you confirm the accuracy of this?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions for this witness. Just one thing, please. I would like to draw your attention to one thing in the record. While my colleague Petrusic was examining the witness, on page 23, line 21, he was talking about a document which contained the name Omer Stambolic which should have been recorded in that way. However, the record is wrong, and it reflects as Momir Stanovic. If this means anything, I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to move for the correction to be made to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the correction will be affected. I thank you, Mr. Sarapa. That concludes the cross-examinations. Is there re-examination, Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: A few questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: For the first question may I ask to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you recall if any of the civilian population in the enclave being killed or injured by Serb actions during 1994 or in 1995, before the final attack?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A citizen by the name of Osman Torlak, but I can't remember whether this was in 1994. It was probably in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you say anything about whether the Serb -- Bosnian Serb forces adhered to the no-firing rule against the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that they mostly did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My objection was about the witness's answer. I was just going to say that he has already answered that question on his examination-in-chief, and one of my questions was whether the Serb forces honoured the cease-fire, and he confirmed that they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you wish to comment on that Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I can move on. I have a couple of other questions, but could I ask -- there is a document I would like to show, which isn't on e-court, but I have a hard copy in a perhaps could be put on the ELMO. I also have copies for the Defence teams in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That arises from which part --

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: It arises, Mr. President in relation to the questions on the smuggling or transport of fuel into the enclave and who might have been controlling that process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's properly in order. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you, please, to --

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: -- read out the text in that document?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not very legible, but I'll try. "Pursuant to your document number 16/18/249, dated 18 June 1995, the needs of the Ukraine units in the sector of Zepa, including foods and fuel should be met. We inform you that in agreement with the commander of the Ukrainian units we have taken five litres, I suppose half of the allowed quantity for the purposes of our brigade, commander Major Rajko Kusic".

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The English translation we've just been given, the official one, is -- has a significant difference to what has just come across in translation. We've heard the word...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, shall we discuss this with the witness removing --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I've got no difficulty with the witness keeping his earphones on. The translation just mentioned the word "food" this translation doesn't mention the word "food" that's the difference. Perhaps it could be clarified, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'll be happy to ask for any portion of it to be reread, or for a copy -- I have a spare copy perhaps that could be given to the translation booth, if that would help.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not sure why my learned friend -- I'm not criticising him, asked the witness to read the document out. Yesterday I was rightly told not to do that by the interpreters because they don't have the advantage of having the official translation in front of them and that's where the difficulty arises.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the word "food" is not in the original text. The interpreter has misheard the witness on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So makes it even more complicated in a way, and resolves the problem. So I take it, and I want a confirmation of this and I'm going to ask the witness again. Witness, when you read this document, is there any mention of food in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In one part it says, "In addition to other goods," which may imply food. This is also a word that can be interpreted as "food."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the English text we have "with other provisions," so that covers it. All right. Are you both happy, Mr. Josse, and Mr. Elderkin, on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I have no further comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could I also ask that the top of the document be shown on the ELMO, just the section that shows the addressee. I'll go ahead and read the English for the sake of clarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Witness, at the top you see that the document is addressed from the commander of the 1st Podrinske LPBR and is dated 23rd of June, 1995. Can I also ask you to see that the document seems to be addressed to General Mladic, indicated of the VRS, the Republika Srpska army. Do you know, or do you recall learning from UNPROFOR troops in the enclave whether the VRS was involved in sanctioning shipments of fuel into the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Objection. Leading question, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a leading question, and you are on recross [sic]. So you may perhaps wish to either drop it completely or rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If I may rephrase, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see how you will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Reading this document, do you know anything about the process by which fuel was authorised to enter the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It arrived in UNPROFOR vehicles to meet their needs. But they also sold certain quantities, I suppose if they had any surplus.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you know if the Serbs were getting any of the fuel?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that they received fuel, but I know that they took certain quantities from all the humanitarian aid convoys and they would keep those quantities for themselves and they would let the rest through to the demilitarised zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask for one last document to be shown to the witness. Again, I'm afraid this is not in e-court. So I have a hard copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: In the document that I showed you just now, there was a reference to order 249 of 18th of June, and the document now on the ELMO is the order with that reference number of 18th of June, 1995. And again, this is a VRS document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could you show, please, the last page at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And this is a document signed, "standing in for Chief of Staff", Colonel Radivoje Miletic. Could I ask to go to the -- I see the second last paragraph is on the screen, so that's fine. If I read out the following in English: "I demand a detailed control of all vehicles, including the inspection of cargo. Pay special attention to the fuel in the tanks, and the fuel being brought into the enclaves. Check the documents and the identity of all persons on board. Make a list of their names and their ID cards in order to ensure that the persons who enter the enclaves must leave the enclaves upon completion of their task."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my objection goes to the part of the Prosecutor's interpretation of this document when he says "stands in for the Chief of Staff." In the handwritten part of the text at the end, those of us who read the text in Serbian, we cannot read this. There is an abbreviation, but it remains for us to interpret that abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to follow like this, because although I can follow what Mr. Elderkin said, I don't know the corresponding word in your language that you are referring to, or the phrase that you are referring to. So you need to indicate that in the first place. He is saying that that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second page of the document, the one that is on the screen now, above the incoming stamp containing dates, there are three handwritten lines. In the first handwritten line it says "standing in for US" or "NS". In other words, this abbreviation could be either "US" or "NS" but the Prosecutor purports that this stands for the Chief of Staff. We can't see it in this document. It's not that clear to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What would "NS" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could agree that this might mean Chief of Staff, but in the course of the examination of the witness yesterday my colleague, Mr. Josse, found himself in a similar situation and he was not allowed to interpret an abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But my question is, what would "NS" stand for? What would "US" stand for?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am telling you that "NS" could stand for Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And "US"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In the staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would "standing in the staff" make any -- any sense? What's the next word, the one in the middle? If anyone can read it for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Colonel."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Colonel," okay. Yes, I see Mr. McCloskey wanting to join in the fun. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This will be an issue that when we get to it will of course be an issue you will get lots of information on. I may have even mentioned this in my opening statement but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't think it should be stated in the presence of the witness. Let's move on, let's proceed. And then of course your position is -- Mr. Petrusic, your position, and that of your client is reserved on this issue. But we do have what purports to be an official translation of this document, which says, "Standing in for Chief of Staff," and we have to proceed on that until we receive proof of the contrary, or evidence to the contrary. Yes, Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If I may return to my questioning of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, I have forgotten what it was, actually. I think you need to return to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I think it would be help if I reread the brief paragraph in order to frame the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I said I don't remember in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to the following paragraph, "I demand a detailed control of all vehicles, including the inspection of cargo, pay special attention to the fuel in the fuel tanks, and the fuel being brought into the enclaves. Check the documents and the identity of all persons on board, make list of their names and their ID cards in order to ensure that the persons who enter the enclaves must leave the enclaves upon completion of the task." Witness, can you tell us if -- what is your understanding of the inspection processes that were carried out on the convoys on the Serb -- Bosnian Serb army side before they arrived in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MEHO DZEBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a very broad question, and it concerns broad authority, but they probably had full control of what was entering and exiting the Zepa demilitarised zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Elderkin. Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, will you allow me to ask some additional questions that concern this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Such as what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The questions would be about whether the witness has any knowledge about the controls being carried out on a regular basis in order to prevent weapons from being illegally brought into the zone. And perhaps there's something that is not included in this list here, so it would be about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think that arises necessarily out of this document. It could have been put, the questions could have been put on cross-examination. And similar questions were put on cross-examinations by others in any case. But I still need to make sure that my colleagues are in agreement with me. Okay. It seems we are unanimous on this. Thank you. Witness, we don't have any further questions for you, which means that you are free to go wherever you wish to go. Our staff will assist you. On behalf of the Trial Chamber and also the Tribunal, I wish to thank you for having come over and for having testified. And on behalf of everyone, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's start with the Prosecution exhibits. Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I would ask to be admitted the witness's statement, P02486, and also the two documents used on redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. They don't seem to have -- it's P02486, ERN in the English 0607-3300 to 3307; B/C/S 3300 to 3307. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence objects, not to the contents of this document, and I think that we can agree with the Prosecution that this signature standing in for the Chief of Staff, Colonel Radivoje Miletic, I think we can agree that this is not the handwriting of Colonel Radivoje Miletic, so it's not his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's no good reason for not admitting. I mean you will have every chance of contesting it in due course. Anyway, these two documents do not have a 65 ter number. So I think we need to refer to the ERN number, and even there I have a difficulty because I have the ERN number for one of them in the B/C/S, but I don't have -- or I can't read because it's not legible, the corresponding ERN in -- for the English version.
